questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.2 - Do I notice needs before I am asked?"

anchors.1: I usually remain unaware until someone asks directly.
anchors.4: I notice obvious needs but miss quieter signals or people outside my usual circle.
anchors.7: Attentive service is increasingly characteristic; I notice patterns, listen, and act appropriately before every need must be announced.

questions.title: Am I personally involved with people who suffer?
questions.prompt: Beyond donations or general concern, how willing am I to spend time, attention, presence, effort, and relationship with people who are lonely, grieving, sick, poor, burdened, or struggling?
questions.christ_example: Christ touched lepers, visited homes, wept with mourners, and entered people's suffering personally (John 11:33-35; Mark 1:40-42).
questions.reflection_prompt: Whose suffering have I kept safely abstract?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.3 - Am I personally involved with people who suffer?"

anchors.1: I prefer helping at a distance and avoid personal involvement with suffering.
anchors.4: I engage personally in some situations but often protect myself from inconvenience or emotional cost.
anchors.7: Personal compassion is increasingly characteristic; I am willing to mourn, comfort, listen, visit, and remain present as appropriate.

questions.title: Is financial generosity a meaningful pattern in my life?
questions.prompt: Within my actual means and responsibilities, how consistently do I willingly use money to relieve need, support good, bless others, and build God's work rather than giving only occasionally or when little sacrifice is required?
questions.christ_example: Christ praised the widow's offering because of the heart and sacrifice represented, not the amount alone (Mark 12:41-44).
questions.reflection_prompt: Does my actual use of money reveal that blessing others matters to me?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.4 - Is financial generosity a meaningful pattern in my life?"

anchors.1: Financial generosity is rare or limited mainly to what costs me almost nothing.
anchors.4: I give meaningfully in some ways but generosity is not yet a consistent stewardship pattern.
anchors.7: Generosity is increasingly characteristic; giving is deliberate, cheerful, proportionate to my circumstances, and responsive to real opportunities.

questions.title: What do I instinctively think abundance is for?
questions.prompt: When I receive more money, time, influence, opportunity, comfort, or capacity, where does my mind naturally go first - only toward more consumption and accumulation, or also toward good I could do?
questions.christ_example: Christ warned against defining life by abundance of possessions (Luke 12:15).
questions.reflection_prompt: When I have more, does my mind naturally move only toward more - or also toward good?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.5 - What do I instinctively think abundance is for?"

anchors.1: More usually produces a desire for still more, with little thought of stewardship beyond myself.
anchors.4: I think about generosity sometimes, but personal consumption and accumulation remain the default.
anchors.7: Stewardship increasingly shapes abundance; I enjoy appropriate blessings while also asking what additional good increased capacity makes possible.

questions.title: Do I use nonfinancial resources to bless others?
questions.prompt: How intentionally do I use time, expertise, tools, property, connections, influence, experience, transportation, hospitality, attention, and other nonfinancial resources for good?
questions.christ_example: Christ used every capacity He possessed in service of the Father's children (Acts 10:38).
questions.reflection_prompt: What resource other than money could I use much more generously?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.6 - Do I use nonfinancial resources to bless others?"

anchors.1: I largely treat these resources as private benefits.
anchors.4: I share them when asked but rarely think proactively about their potential to bless.
anchors.7: Stewardship is increasingly characteristic; I see many resources as tools God can use through me to bless His children.

questions.title: Do I give only from what is left over?
questions.prompt: How consistently do I make meaningful room in my life and resources for generosity and service rather than helping primarily when I happen to have time, money, energy, or other resources left over?
questions.christ_example: Christ sometimes allowed planned rest to be interrupted by compassion, while also appropriately withdrawing to rest and pray (Mark 6:30-34; Luke 5:16).
questions.reflection_prompt: If someone saw only how I allocate my time and resources, would they know serving and blessing others matter to me?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.7 - Do I give only from what is left over?"

anchors.1: Service and generosity receive mainly leftovers after my own wants and plans.
anchors.4: I make room in some areas, but generosity is easily displaced by competing preferences.
anchors.7: Intentional generosity is increasingly characteristic; I prayerfully make meaningful room within real responsibilities to bless others and do good, rather than consistently giving God and His children only what remains.

questions.title: When I cannot meet a need, does compassion remain?
questions.prompt: When I genuinely cannot or should not provide the requested help, how consistently do I preserve compassion, dignity, prayer, and willingness to help in another appropriate way rather than hardening my heart?
questions.christ_example: Christ did not meet every temporal need in every place, yet His compassion was constant and His actions followed the Father's will (Mark 1:35-38).
questions.reflection_prompt: The goal is not unlimited giving; it is a heart that does not use limitation as an excuse for indifference.
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "10.8 - When I cannot meet a need, does compassion remain?"

anchors.1: If I cannot solve the problem, I often emotionally dismiss the person or need.
anchors.4: I care but may withdraw quickly when I cannot provide the obvious solution.
anchors.7: Compassion remains even when resources or wisdom limit action; I can say no appropriately without becoming indifferent.

questions.title: Do I truly pray - and keep a prayer in my heart?
questions.prompt: During the past seven days, how consistently did I engage in sincere, focused personal prayer and also seek to keep my heart turned toward Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ throughout the day - expressing gratitude, seeking help and guidance, sharing concerns and desires, listening for the Holy Ghost, and including Them in ordinary experiences and decisions?
questions.christ_example: Christ frequently withdrew for focused prayer and also lived in continual communion with the Father (Luke 5:16; 6:12; John 17).
questions.reflection_prompt: Focused prayer means I stop and give God attention; a prayerful heart means I do not say amen and disconnect for the next twelve hours.
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.1 - Do I truly pray - and keep a prayer in my heart?"

anchors.1: Prayer is infrequent, rushed, mechanical, or largely disconnected from the rest of my day.
anchors.4: I pray regularly but depth, listening, or continuing prayerfulness varies considerably.
anchors.7: Prayerful communion with God is increasingly characteristic: I make time for sincere focused prayer and seek to keep my heart drawn out to Him throughout the day.

questions.title: Do I feast upon the words of Christ - or merely read them?
questions.prompt: How consistently do I approach scripture and inspired teaching seeking to know Jesus Christ, understand His will, ponder deeply, ask questions, study important words and context, connect related teachings, seek the Holy Ghost, and apply what I learn?
questions.christ_example: Christ knew, quoted, interpreted, and lived scripture as the word of His Father (Matthew 4:1-11; Luke 4:16-21).
questions.reflection_prompt: Is my study producing knowledge about scripture, or helping me come unto Christ and live differently?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.2 - Do I feast upon the words of Christ - or merely read them?"

anchors.1: Scripture engagement is rare, superficial, or mainly about completing a reading task.
anchors.4: I study regularly and sometimes ponder deeply, but application and seeking revelation are inconsistent.
anchors.7: Feasting upon the words of Christ is increasingly characteristic; study leads to understanding, revelation, repentance, changed decisions, and deeper knowledge of Christ.

questions.title: Do I examine myself and repent daily?
questions.prompt: How consistently do I prayerfully examine my life - preferably each day - asking Heavenly Father to help me recognize not only sins and wrong choices, but also sins of omission, missed opportunities to do good, harmful patterns, weaknesses, and ways I am falling short of following Jesus Christ; and then specifically repent, repair, and seek the Savior's grace to change?
questions.christ_example: Christ repeatedly invited people not merely to feel regret but to repent and follow Him (John 8:11; Luke 5:32).
questions.reflection_prompt: Repentance is not merely feeling bad about yesterday. It is turning toward Christ so tomorrow can become different.
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.3 - Do I examine myself and repent daily?"

anchors.1: Self-examination and specific repentance are infrequent; I tend to wait for obvious problems.
anchors.4: I repent regularly but often in broad terms or after consequences make a problem obvious.
anchors.7: Daily repentance is increasingly characteristic; I ask God what I am not seeing, acknowledge wrong without excuse, repair what I can, and rely on Christ to change behavior, desires, and character.

questions.title: Do I withdraw from distraction to seek God?
questions.prompt: In a life filled with activity, information, entertainment, responsibilities, and noise, how consistently do I deliberately step away from unnecessary distraction to pray, ponder, examine my life, remember Jesus Christ, study His words, and become sufficiently still and attentive to receive guidance from the Holy Ghost?
questions.christ_example: Christ repeatedly withdrew to solitary places to pray, sometimes for extended periods (Mark 1:35; Luke 5:16; 6:12).
questions.reflection_prompt: Stillness itself is not the virtue. Seeking God is the virtue; stillness can make concentrated seeking possible.
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.4 - Do I withdraw from distraction to seek God?"

anchors.1: I rarely create undistracted space for God; noise and stimulation fill nearly every available moment.
anchors.4: I sometimes seek quiet spiritual space but it is easily displaced by devices, work, entertainment, or busyness.
anchors.7: Intentional spiritual stillness is increasingly characteristic; I regularly withdraw from unnecessary noise for concentrated seeking of God.

questions.title: Do I truly keep the Sabbath day holy?
questions.prompt: How consistently do I intentionally keep the Sabbath day holy by worshipping Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ, preparing for and worthily partaking of the sacrament, participating in Church meetings, resting appropriately from ordinary work and worldly pursuits, strengthening family and others, serving where appropriate, studying and pondering the gospel, and choosing activities that make the day a genuine sign of devotion to God?
questions.christ_example: Christ worshipped on the Sabbath and taught that the day is for God's purposes and doing good, not Pharisaic rule-making (Luke 4:16; Mark 2:27; 3:1-5).
questions.reflection_prompt: If someone could observe only how I use the Sabbath, what would my choices suggest about the place Jesus Christ occupies in my life?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.5 - Do I truly keep the Sabbath day holy?"

anchors.1: The Sabbath is often little different from other days or is shaped mainly by convenience and entertainment.
anchors.4: I attend and observe many Sabbath practices, but the day is inconsistently centered on worship, renewal, and devotion.
anchors.7: Keeping the Sabbath holy is increasingly characteristic; I receive it as a sacred gift, distinguish it from other days, worship sincerely, seek the Spirit, strengthen others, and let it re-center my life on Christ.

questions.title: Do my spiritual practices actually change how I live?
questions.prompt: To what extent are prayer, scripture study, worship, repentance, temple worship, Sabbath observance, and other spiritual practices actually influencing my desires, priorities, decisions, relationships, repentance, and behavior rather than remaining largely separate from the way I live the rest of my life?
questions.christ_example: Christ taught that hearing His sayings matters when we do them (Matthew 7:24).
questions.reflection_prompt: Did these practices actually bring me to Jesus Christ? Am I becoming different?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "11.6 - Do my spiritual practices actually change how I live?"

anchors.1: My spiritual practices and ordinary behavior often exist in separate compartments.
anchors.4: My practices influence some areas of life, but repeated insights do not consistently become changed behavior.
anchors.7: Transformative discipleship is increasingly characteristic; spiritual practices bring me to Christ, help me hear the Holy Ghost, expose what must change, and lead to observable changes in how I think, choose, love, serve, repent, and live.

questions.title: Am I deliberately walking with Jesus Christ on the covenant path?
questions.prompt: How intentionally do I seek to understand, remember, and live the covenants I have made through baptism, priesthood ordination, and temple ordinances - and the regular renewal of my covenants through the partaking of the sacrament - as parts of an ongoing covenant relationship with Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ, pondering what those covenants mean in my present life and seeking personal revelation about how to faithfully live them?
questions.christ_example: Christ invited disciples into an enduring relationship of following, remembering, and abiding in Him (John 15:4-10).
questions.reflection_prompt: Are my covenants increasingly becoming part of who I am, not merely ordinances I once received?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.1 - Am I deliberately walking with Jesus Christ on the covenant path?"

questions.title: Do I meaningfully renew my covenants through the sacrament?
questions.prompt: When I partake of the sacrament, how intentionally do I remember Jesus Christ and His Atonement, examine my life, renew my willingness to take His name upon me, always remember Him, keep His commandments, and seek the promised blessing of having His Spirit with me?
questions.christ_example: The resurrected Christ personally instituted the sacrament among the Nephites and commanded them to remember Him (3 Nephi 18:1-12).
questions.reflection_prompt: Has the sacrament become a living weekly covenant experience, or mainly a familiar ritual?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.2 - Do I meaningfully renew my covenants through the sacrament?"

questions.title: Do I return to the temple to learn, remember, worship, serve, and receive revelation?
questions.prompt: Within my circumstances and reasonable access, how intentionally do I return to the temple - not merely to attend, but to worship Jesus Christ, remember and better understand the covenants I have made, seek the teaching of the Holy Ghost, receive personal revelation, serve those who have died, and strengthen my commitment to live those covenants outside the temple?
questions.christ_example: Jesus called the temple His Father's house and treated it as sacred (John 2:16).
questions.reflection_prompt: What is temple worship changing in me outside the temple?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.3 - Do I return to the temple to learn, remember, worship, serve, and receive revelation?"

questions.title: Law of Obedience: Is my will increasingly aligned with God's will?
questions.prompt: As I seek to live the law of obedience, how intentionally do I strive to know and keep God's commandments - not merely when they are convenient or agree with what I already want, but because I love and trust Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ and desire to align my will with Theirs?
questions.christ_example: Jesus Christ perfectly aligned His will with the Father: 'not my will, but thine, be done' (Luke 22:42).
questions.reflection_prompt: When God's will differs from mine, which one am I trying to change?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.4 - Law of Obedience: Is my will increasingly aligned with God's will?"

questions.title: Law of Sacrifice: Am I offering the Lord a broken heart and a contrite spirit?
questions.prompt: As I seek to live the law of sacrifice, how intentionally do I offer Jesus Christ a broken heart and a contrite spirit - humbly recognizing my dependence upon Him, sincerely repenting, submitting my will to His, and becoming willing to give up or subordinate whatever He asks of me in order to follow Him and support His work?
questions.christ_example: Jesus Christ's submission in Gethsemane is the perfect pattern of yielding heart and will to the Father (Luke 22:42).
questions.reflection_prompt: The deepest question may not be 'What am I willing to give up?' but 'How completely am I willing to give my heart and will to Jesus Christ?'
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.5 - Law of Sacrifice: Am I offering the Lord a broken heart and a contrite spirit?"

questions.title: Law of the Gospel of Jesus Christ: Am I actually living His gospel?
questions.prompt: As I seek to live the law of the gospel of Jesus Christ, how intentionally am I exercising faith in Him, repenting and continually coming unto Him, receiving and honoring the ordinances and covenants God offers me, keeping His commandments, seeking the sanctifying influence of the Holy Ghost, enduring faithfully to the end, and relying upon the Atonement and grace of Jesus Christ to become more like Him and ultimately be perfected in Him?
questions.christ_example: Jesus declared, 'this is the gospel which I have given unto you' and taught the path that leads us to stand spotless before Him (3 Nephi 27:13-21).
questions.reflection_prompt: Rather than attempting to define every element of the law of the gospel, consider the scriptural pattern and ask: Is the gospel something I believe - or increasingly the way I live?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.6 - Law of the Gospel of Jesus Christ: Am I actually living His gospel?"

questions.title: Law of Chastity: Is my sexuality governed by my covenant relationship with God?
questions.prompt: As I seek to live the law of chastity, how intentionally do I keep my sexual conduct within the boundaries God has established and seek purity in my thoughts, desires, media choices, relationships, and treatment of others - viewing sexuality as a sacred part of discipleship rather than an area separated from my covenant relationship with Him?
questions.christ_example: Christ taught chastity of heart as well as outward conduct (Matthew 5:27-28).
questions.reflection_prompt: Involuntary temptation, thought, feeling, or attraction is not itself what is being assessed. Consider what you voluntarily entertain, cultivate, seek, and choose.
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.7 - Law of Chastity: Is my sexuality governed by my covenant relationship with God?"

questions.title: Law of Consecration: Does everything I have increasingly belong to God?
questions.prompt: As I seek to live the law of consecration, how intentionally do I regard my time, talents, abilities, influence, opportunities, material resources, and everything else the Lord has blessed me with as ultimately entrusted by Him - and seek personal revelation about how He would have me use them to build His kingdom, bless His children, relieve suffering, and accomplish His purposes?
questions.christ_example: Christ held nothing back from the Father's work and ultimately gave His whole life (John 10:17-18; 17:4).
questions.reflection_prompt: What has God entrusted to me? What am I attached to? What opportunities am I overlooking? What are my motives? What do I believe He is asking me to do?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.8 - Law of Consecration: Does everything I have increasingly belong to God?"

questions.title: Are my family relationships increasingly shaped by God's plan and my covenants with Him?
questions.prompt: How intentionally do I understand my family relationships and responsibilities within God's plan of happiness and allow my covenants with Him to shape the way I love, serve, sacrifice for, remain faithful to, teach, strengthen, forgive, and build relationships with those He has entrusted most closely to me? If I have made sealing covenants, how meaningfully does the eternal and covenant nature of my marriage affect how I treat my spouse, resolve differences, establish priorities, sacrifice, remain faithful, and seek to build a Christ-centered eternal relationship?
questions.christ_example: Christ honored family responsibilities, taught covenant faithfulness, and used marriage imagery to teach enduring covenant relationship (John 19:26-27; Matthew 19:4-6).
questions.reflection_prompt: Do the people closest to me experience my covenants through the way I actually love and live?
questions.source_locator: docx heading: "12.9 - Are my family relationships increasingly shaped by God's plan and my covenants with Him?"
